questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Engineering & Discrete Mathematics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: If A is a 3×3 matrix with eigenvalues 2, -3, and 5, what is the trace of A^2 + 2I?
questions.explanationEn: Eigenvalues of A^2 + 2I are λ^2 + 2: 2^2+2 = 6, (-3)^2+2 = 11, and 5^2+2 = 27. Trace equals the sum of eigenvalues: 6 + 11 + 27 = 44.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Engineering & Discrete Mathematics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: Let P(x, y) mean 'x trusts y' over the domain of all people. Which formula expresses 'Everyone trusts someone who does not trust themselves'?
questions.explanationEn: 'Everyone' requires ∀x outside, and 'someone' (which may depend on x) requires ∃y inside such that P(x, y) and ¬P(y, y) both hold.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Engineering & Discrete Mathematics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: On a set A with n = 3 elements, how many reflexive relations exist?
questions.explanationEn: All n = 3 diagonal pairs (a, a) must be included (1 choice each). The remaining n^2 - n = 6 off-diagonal pairs can each be included or excluded: 2^6 = 64 reflexive relations.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Engineering & Discrete Mathematics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: If f: A -> B is injective (one-to-one) and |A| = 5, |B| = 7, how many such injective functions exist?
questions.explanationEn: An injective function assigns distinct elements of B to each of the 5 elements of A: 7 * 6 * 5 * 4 * 3 = P(7, 5) = 2520.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Engineering & Discrete Mathematics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about a finite lattice (L, <=) is/are ALWAYS TRUE?
optionsEn: L has a unique least element and a unique greatest element.
Every pair of elements in L has a unique greatest lower bound (meet) and least upper bound (join).
Every totally ordered finite set is a lattice.
questions.explanationEn: Every lattice has unique meet and join for every pair (B), every finite lattice is bounded with unique min and max (A), and every chain/total order is a lattice (D). Not all finite lattices are distributive (e.g., M_3 and N_5), so (C) is false.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Engineering & Discrete Mathematics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: What is the rank of the 3×3 matrix [[1, 2, 3], [2, 4, 6], [1, 1, 1]]?
questions.explanationEn: Row 2 is 2 * Row 1, so it is linearly dependent. Row 1 and Row 3 are linearly independent. Therefore, the rank is 2.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Engineering & Discrete Mathematics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: By the Mean Value Theorem, for f(x) = x^2 on [1, 5], what is the value of c in (1, 5) such that f'(c) = (f(5) - f(1)) / (5 - 1)?

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Engineering & Discrete Mathematics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: What is the value of lim_{n -> ∞} (1 + 3/n)^(2n)?
questions.explanationEn: Using lim_{n -> ∞} (1 + a/n)^(bn) = e^(ab), here a = 3 and b = 2, giving e^(3*2) = e^6.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Engineering & Discrete Mathematics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: For any three sets A, B, and C, which of the following set identities ALWAYS hold?
questions.explanationEn: All four are valid set identities: distributivity of ∩ over ∪ (A), De Morgan's laws for set difference (B, C), and distributivity of Cartesian product over union (D).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Engineering & Discrete Mathematics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: What is the chromatic number of the complete bipartite graph K_{4, 7}?
questions.explanationEn: Every non-empty bipartite graph with at least one edge can be properly colored with 2 colors (one color per bipartition set) and requires at least 2 colors. Hence χ(K_{4,7}) = 2.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Engineering & Discrete Mathematics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: What is the value of ∫_0^∞ x^2 * e^(-x) dx?
questions.explanationEn: By the Gamma function definition, ∫_0^∞ x^n e^(-x) dx = Γ(n + 1) = n!. For n = 2, 2! = 2.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Engineering & Discrete Mathematics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following series CONVERGE?
questions.explanationEn: (A) converges (p-series with p=2 > 1). (B) is the harmonic series (diverges). (C) is the alternating harmonic series (converges conditionally by Leibniz test). (D) converges by ratio test (ratio -> 1/2 < 1).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Engineering & Discrete Mathematics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: Let A and B be two events with P(A) = 0.4 and P(B) = 0.6. Which of the following inequalities MUST hold regardless of whether A and B are independent?
questions.explanationEn: Since A ∩ B ⊆ A, P(A ∩ B) <= min(0.4, 0.6) = 0.4, and since P(A)+P(B)=1.0, P(A ∩ B) >= 0 (A). P(A ∪ B) >= max(0.4, 0.6) = 0.6 and <= 1 (B). By De Morgan, P(A^c ∪ B^c) = 1 - P(A ∩ B) >= 1 - 0.4 = 0.6 (D). (C) only holds if independent.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Engineering & Discrete Mathematics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: What is the value of the definite integral ∫_0^π x * sin(x) dx? (Rounded to two decimal places, use π = 3.1416)
questions.explanationEn: Integration by parts: u = x, dv = sin(x)dx => [-x*cos(x)]_0^π + ∫_0^π cos(x)dx = (-π*(-1) - 0) + [sin(x)]_0^π = π + 0 = π ≈ 3.14.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Engineering & Discrete Mathematics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: Consider f(x) = x^3 - 3x^2 - 9x + 5 on R. Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
optionsEn: f has an inflection point at x = 1.
f has a local maximum at x = -1.
f has a local minimum at x = 3.
questions.explanationEn: f'(x) = 3x^2 - 6x - 9 = 3(x - 3)(x + 1) = 0 at x = -1, 3. f''(x) = 6x - 6: f''(-1) = -12 < 0 (local max, A), f''(3) = 12 > 0 (local min, B), f''(1) = 0 with sign change (inflection point, C). On (-1, 3), f'(x) < 0 so f is decreasing.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Engineering & Discrete Mathematics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn:
For what value of λ does the homogeneous system:
  x + 2y + z = 0
  2x + λy + 2z = 0
  3x + 6y + λz = 0
have a non-trivial solution?
questions.explanationEn: Determinant of coefficient matrix: R2 -> R2 - 2R1 gives [0, λ-4, 0]; R3 -> R3 - 3R1 gives [0, 0, λ-3]. Upper triangular determinant = 1*(λ - 4)*(λ - 3) = 0 => λ = 4 or λ = 3.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Engineering & Discrete Mathematics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following propositional formulas is/are logically equivalent to (p -> q)?
questions.explanationEn: p -> q is equivalent to ¬p ∨ q (implication law), ¬q -> ¬p (contrapositive), and ¬(p ∧ ¬q) (De Morgan on ¬p ∨ q). Its converse (q -> p) is not equivalent.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Engineering & Discrete Mathematics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: Let G be a simple connected undirected graph with n >= 3 vertices. Which of the following conditions is/are SUFFICIENT to guarantee that G has a Hamiltonian cycle?
optionsEn: Every vertex has degree at least n/2.
For every pair of non-adjacent vertices u and v, deg(u) + deg(v) >= n.
questions.explanationEn: Dirac's Theorem (A) and Ore's Theorem (B) are sufficient conditions for a Hamiltonian cycle. Even degrees (C) guarantee an Eulerian circuit (not Hamiltonian), and 2-connectivity (D) is necessary but not sufficient (e.g., K_{2,3}).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Engineering & Discrete Mathematics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: Let A be a 3×3 matrix such that A^2 = A (idempotent). Which of the following statements is/are ALWAYS TRUE?
optionsEn: Every eigenvalue of A is either 0 or 1.
questions.explanationEn: If Av = λv, then A^2 v = λ^2 v = λv => λ ∈ {0, 1} (A). Idempotent matrices are diagonalizable over {0, 1}, so trace(A) = sum of 1-eigenvalues = rank(A) (B). Also (I - A)^2 = I - 2A + A^2 = I - A (D). Only A = I is invertible (C false).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Engineering & Discrete Mathematics (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: How many spanning trees does the complete bipartite graph K_{2, 4} have?
questions.explanationEn: The number of spanning trees of K_{m, n} is m^(n-1) * n^(m-1). For m = 2, n = 4: 2^(4-1) * 4^(2-1) = 2^3 * 4^1 = 8 * 4 = 32.
